reason: The cited evidence directly shows that rapid quenching produces an amorphous structure while slow cooling yields crystalline phases, and states that phosphorus enhances glass-forming ability. However, the evidence does not compare the thermal stability (crystallization onset temperature) of the amorphous versus crystalline states, so the premise of improved thermal stability is unsupported.
premises: Rapid quenching (10^5–10^6 K/s) of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 yields an amorphous structure
Slow cooling (~52 K/s) of the same alloy yields a complex crystalline microstructure
Phosphorus addition enhances glass-forming ability during rapid cooling
The amorphous state exhibits higher thermal stability (delayed crystallization) than the crystalline state
